text: 58-year-old male. The patient reports a year-long history of burning pain in his neck and arms, accompanying paresthesias in his hands. speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Cervical Spondylotic Myelopathy.

The patient's 58-year-old male with a one-year history of burning neck pain, paresthesias in the hands, and progressive bilateral hand weakness over three months is highly suggestive of cervical myelopathy, likely secondary to degenerative disc disease and osteoarthritis. His history of diabetes, hypertension, and hypercholesterolemia are significant comorbidities that may affect recovery or indicate vascular contributions, but the clinical picture of progressive upper motor neuron signs (weakness) combined with sensory symptoms points strongly to cervical cord compression.

Please confirm if you have noticed any difficulty with fine motor tasks like buttoning shirts or holding objects, and whether you have experienced balance problems or clumsiness in your legs. Also, have you noticed any bowel or bladder changes?
